text:
noah (sales): Quick sync - ClinicHealth needs a concise POC runbook + cost sketch for their on-prem validation. Requirements: sustain 200 r/s with ~64 tokens output, p95 < 300ms, and measure cold-starts during scale events. Theywant to run tests in their air-gapped site if possible.

maria (solutions): We should offer two paths: 1) provide an offline package + test harness they run locally, or 2) run a short ephemeral Dedicated pool in their cloud VNet then mirror to on-prem. Which do we prefer?

devon (eng-ml): Either works. For reproducible perf numbers the Dedicated pool is easier (less infra variance). For PHI concerns, the offline package is fine if they can run the harness. We'll give them both options and a recommended default.

akash (eng-runtime): Recommended hardware: 8x A100-equivalent across 2 nodes (4 GPUs/node) with concurrency_per_gpu=4. With int8 quantization and prefix cache we hit ~200 r/s with batching tuned.

noah (sales): They also want a simple pricing line so their procurement can greenlight the test. Keep it high-level.

maria (solutions): Draft pricing lines: infra rental: $X/hr per GPU (list) -> 8 GPUs -> hours. Managed support: flat fee for POC support. Also show token-cost estimate for a full-24h run and for our recommended 12h steady POC.

devon (eng-ml): Token calc: 200 r/s * 3600s * 12h * 64 tokens = 552,960,000 tokens for 12h. If we quote $0.00035/token => ~$193k for token bill; include note that token pricing is illustrative. Emphasize POC will be less (we run in blocks, not full 12h continuous at peak).

noah (sales): Good. Can we give them a runnable test plan for their engineers (k6 + simple capture) and a CSV schema for results?

maria (solutions): I'll author the runbook. Key pieces: pre-warm cache, steady blocks, stress spike, cold-start rotation, logs to collect.

devon (eng-ml): k6 snippet (arrival-rate style) to approximate target rps:

```js
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';

export let options = {
  scenarios: {
    steady: {
      executor: 'constant-arrival-rate',
      rate: 200,
      timeUnit: '1s',
      duration: '12m',
      preAllocatedVUs: 150,
      maxVUs: 300
    }
  },
  thresholds: { 'http_req_duration': ['p(95)<300'] }
};

export default function () {
  const body = JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-13b', input: 'Summarize clinical note', max_tokens: 64 });
  const params = { headers: { 'Content-Type':'application/json', 'Authorization': `Bearer ${__ENV.API_KEY}` } };
  http.post('https://localhost:8443/v1/generate', body, params);
  sleep(0.02);
}
```

devon (eng-ml): Notes: use constant-arrival-rate to get steady RPS. Warmup: run the scenario for 3 minutes at 25% target, then full steady runs. Capture k6 summary JSON (--out json=summary.json).

akash (eng-runtime): Runtime config suggestion (redwood.yaml):

```yaml
model: redwood-13b
quantize: int8
prefix_cache: true
batching:
  max_batch_size: 64
  batch_timeout_ms: 6
concurrency_per_gpu: 4
metrics_export: prometheus
```

akash (eng-runtime): Cold-start test: rotate a node via systemctl restart redwood-node.service (or container restart). After restart, send 10 sequential requests and record latencies. Repeat for each node.

sophia (security): For the on-prem/offline option, include these points for their compliance team:
- Control plane can be deployed customer-side (no telemetry leaves network)
- Keys can stay in their KMS/HSM; we support customer-managed keys
- Audit logs are local and can be exported to their SIEM
- We will provide SOC2 docs under NDA and a short security Q&A template

noah (sales): Good. Include those bullets in the runbook and a one-page security appendix. Also they asked: can we lock model versions and prevent automatic updates?

maria (solutions): Yes. We support model pinning and an offline approval manifest. We'll give an example manifest and instructions to apply it.

noah (sales): What CSV schema should they upload for post-run analysis?

maria (solutions): Minimal CSV columns: run_id, node_id, timestamp, request_id, status_code, wall_ms, model_tokens_out, batch_size, cpu_pct, gpu_util_pct, kv_cache_hit (true/false). We'll provide a template.

devon (eng-ml): Quick wrk example for rapid local load checks:

```
wrk -t8 -c300 -d60s -s post.lua https://localhost:8443/v1/generate
```

devon (eng-ml): post.lua should set Content-Type and Authorization header and a JSON body. wrk is useful for pushing RPS but doesn't capture per-request percentiles as well as k6.

noah (sales): Deployment bot says ephemeral Dedicated is ready for a smoke run this afternoon. Share baseline numbers and we'll forward the runbook.

deploy-bot: ephemeral-dedicated-clinic-17690: pool created (2 nodes, 4 gpus/node). status: provisioning

akash (eng-runtime): Baseline numbers from internal run: at target cfg we saw p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 290ms, p99 ~ 420ms at steady 200 r/s with prefix cache enabled. With prefix cache disabled p95 moved to ~420ms. Will include raw metrics dump.

sophia (security): I'll attach the NDA link and SOC2 request steps in the outgoing email thread.

maria (solutions): Draft runbook uploaded to the shared drive (link pasted to client). It includes the k6 scripts, wrk examples, redwood.yaml sample, CSV template, and a short troubleshooting checklist.

noah (sales): Great, action items: Maria finalize runbook + CSV; Akash attach config + baseline dumps; Sophia attach security appendix and SOC2 access steps; Devon add k6/wrk snippets. I'll send the email with schedule options. :rocket:

maria (solutions): Will do, aiming to send by EOD PST.

akash (eng-runtime): Pool is healthy, starting a 30-minute validation run now. I'll open a separate thread with the final 12-hour results once complete.

noah (sales): Thanks all. ClinicHealth wants a Tuesday slot, so let's be ready to handoff the runbook and support notes.

deploy-bot: ephemeral-dedicated-clinic-17690: node-1 ready, node-2 ready, pool healthy
